title: Prakrama 3, Sarga 1. The Words of the Women of Kantakanagara
html:
Damodara asks Murari to tell of the Lord's sannyasa; verses of invocation; the Lord leaves Navadvipa; Chandrashekhara returns and tells how the people of Kantakanagara gazed at the Lord and what the women said of Him

Verse 1

श्रुत्वा हरेः कथनमद्भुतमप्रपञ्चं
दामोदरः पुनरुवाच वरं मुरारिम्।
तत्कथ्यतां कथमसौ भगवांश्चकार
न्यासं विदेशगमनं पुरुषोत्तमं च॥१॥

śrutvā hareḥ kathanamadbhutamaprapañcaṁ
dāmodaraḥ punaruvāca varaṁ murārim|
tatkathyatāṁ kathamasau bhagavāṁścakāra
nyāsaṁ videśagamanaṁ puruṣottamaṁ ca||1||

shrutva — having heard; hareh — about Hari; kathanam — the account; adbhutam — wondrous; aprapancham — not of this world; damodarah — Damodara; punah — again; uvacha — said; varam — to the excellent; murarim — Murari; tat — that; kathyatam — let it be told; katham — how; asau — He; bhagavan — Bhagavan; chakara — accomplished; nyasam — sannyasa; videsha-gamanam — travel to other lands; purushottamam — (the journey to) Purushottama; cha — and.

1Having heard the wondrous, unworldly account of Hari, Damodara1 spoke again to the excellent Murari: "Tell, then, how Bhagavan took sannyasa, how He went to other lands and to Purushottama2,

Verse 2

दृष्ट्वा जगाम मुनिसङ्घनिषेवितानि
तीर्थानि कानि च मनोज्ञकृपः पुराणः।
श्रुत्वा वचो द्विजवरस्य जगाद वैद्यो
हृद्यां कथां शृणु हरेः कथयामि तुभ्यम्॥२॥

dṛṣṭvā jagāma munisaṅghaniṣevitāni
tīrthāni kāni ca manojñakṛpaḥ purāṇaḥ|
śrutvā vaco dvijavarasya jagāda vaidyo
hṛdyāṁ kathāṁ śṛṇu hareḥ kathayāmi tubhyam||2||

drishtva — to see; jagama — visited; muni-sangha-nishevitani — frequented by hosts of sages; tirthani — holy places; kani — which; cha — and; manojna-kripah — of charming compassion; puranah — the Ancient One; shrutva — hearing; vachah — the words; dvija-varasya — of the best of the twice-born; jagada — said; vaidyah — the physician; hridyam — dear to the heart; katham — the account; shrinu — hear; hareh — of Hari; kathayami — I shall tell; tubhyam — to you.

2and which holy places, beloved of hosts of sages, the Ancient One, whose compassion charms the heart, went to see." Hearing the words of the best of the twice-born, the physician replied, "Listen, and I shall tell you the heart-delighting account of Hari.

Verse 3

तत्राशु शक्तिमतुलां भगवान्ददातु
वक्तुं यथा मम भवेत्कुशला सुवाणी।
यस्याद्भुतश्रुतिसुधारसनैः सुवाणी
यन्नामसंस्मृतिरसाद्विवशा विमुक्तिः॥३॥

tatrāśu śaktimatulāṁ bhagavāndadātu
vaktuṁ yathā mama bhavetkuśalā suvāṇī|
yasyādbhutaśrutisudhārasanaiḥ suvāṇī
yannāmasaṁsmṛtirasādvivaśā vimuktiḥ||3||

tatra — for this; ashu — soon; shaktim — power; atulam — incomparable; bhagavan — Bhagavan; dadatu — may give; vaktum — to tell; yatha — so that; mama — my; bhavet — may become; kushala — skilled; su-vani — fair speech; yasya — whose; adbhuta-shruti-sudha-rasanaih — by tasting the nectar of hearing (His) wonders; su-vani — speech is fair; yat-nama-samsmriti-rasat — from the sweetness of remembering whose name; vivasha — helplessly (unbidden); vimuktih — liberation.

3May Bhagavan soon grant me incomparable power, so that my speech may be skilled in telling of Him — of Him whose wondrous deeds, when their nectar is tasted by the ear, make speech fair, and from the sweetness of remembering whose name liberation comes of itself, unbidden3.

Verse 4

तं नित्यविग्रहमजं वरहेमगौरं
चैतन्यदेवममलं पुरुषं भजामि।
यत्पादपद्मनखरद्युतिरञ्जितेन
चित्तेन शुद्धमनसः सहसा विदुस्तत्॥४॥

taṁ nityavigrahamajaṁ varahemagauraṁ
caitanyadevamamalaṁ puruṣaṁ bhajāmi|
yatpādapadmanakharadyutirañjitena
cittena śuddhamanasaḥ sahasā vidustat||4||

tam — Him; nitya-vigraham — of eternal form; ajam — unborn; vara-hema-gauram — golden like the finest gold; chaitanya-devam — Chaitanyadeva; amalam — spotless; purusham — the Person; bhajami — I worship; yat-pada-padma-nakhara-dyuti-ranjitena — tinged by the radiance of the nails of whose lotus feet; chittena — with a heart; shuddha-manasah — the pure-minded; sahasa — at once; viduh — know; tat — That.

4I worship Him — Chaitanyadeva, the spotless Person, unborn, eternal in form, golden like the finest gold. The pure-minded, whose hearts are tinged by the radiance of the nails of His lotus feet, at once come to know the Truth.

Verse 5

ब्रह्मस्वभावभगवद्भजनामृतं च
तं देववृन्दपरिवन्दितपादमीडे।
यत्पादपद्ममकरन्दमजस्रं पीत्वा
श्रीशङ्करोऽपि भगवाननुरागपूर्णः॥५॥

brahmasvabhāvabhagavadbhajanāmṛtaṁ ca
taṁ devavṛndaparivanditapādamīḍe|
yatpādapadmamakarandamajasraṁ pītvā
śrīśaṅkaro'pi bhagavānanurāgapūrṇaḥ||5||

brahma-svabhava-bhagavat-bhajana-amritam — the nectar of the worship of Bhagavan, whose nature is Brahman; cha — and; tam — Him; deva-vrinda-parivandita-padam — whose feet are revered by hosts of gods; ide — I praise; yat-pada-padma-makarandam — the honey of whose lotus feet; ajasram — unceasingly; pitva — drinking; shri-shankarah — Sri Shankara (Shiva); api — even; bhagavan — the lord; anuraga-purnah — is filled with love.

5I praise the nectar of the worship of Bhagavan, whose nature is Brahman4, and Him whose feet are revered by hosts of gods: even the lord Sri Shankara5, drinking unceasingly the honey of His lotus feet, is filled with love.

Verse 6

एवं च वैद्यमुपदिश्य निजाश्रयं स
गत्वा स्वभक्तगणसेवनजानुशक्त्या।
शान्तश्च सर्वरसिकेश्वरगौरचन्द्रो
मुग्धं निनाय रजनीं च तदुत्थितोऽगात्॥६॥

evaṁ ca vaidyamupadiśya nijāśrayaṁ sa
gatvā svabhaktagaṇasevanajānuśaktyā|
śāntaśca sarvarasikeśvaragauracandro
mugdhaṁ nināya rajanīṁ ca tadutthito'gāt||6||

evam — thus; cha — and; vaidyam — the physician; upadishya — having instructed; nija-ashrayam — to His own abode; sah — He; gatva — going; sva-bhakta-gana-sevana-ja-anushaktya — with the attachment born of His devotees' service; shantah — calm; cha — and; sarva-rasika-ishvara-gaurachandrah — Gaurachandra, lord of all rasikas; mugdham — in rapture; ninaya — spent; rajanim — the night; cha — and; tat-utthitah — rising after it; agat — departed.

6Having thus instructed the physician, the Lord went home, full of the tenderness that His devotees' service awakens in Him. Calm, Gaurachandra, the lord of all rasikas, spent the night in rapture, and rising, He departed.

Verse 7

उत्तीर्य दिव्यतटिनीं भगवाञ्जगाम
ज्ञात्वाथ खिन्नमनसो द्विजवर्यमुख्याः।
वैक्लव्यमापुरतुलं रुरुदुश्च तप्ताः
शोकार्दिता विमनसोऽतिक्लेशा बभूवुः॥७॥

uttīrya divyataṭinīṁ bhagavāñjagāma
jñātvātha khinnamanaso dvijavaryamukhyāḥ|
vaiklavyamāpuratulaṁ ruruduśca taptāḥ
śokārditā vimanaso'tikleśā babhūvuḥ||7||

uttirya — crossing; divya-tatinim — the divine river; bhagavan — Bhagavan; jagama — went away; jnatva — learning; atha — then; khinna-manasah — downcast; dvija-varya-mukhyah — the chief of the best of the twice-born; vaiklavyam — dismay; apuh — fell into; atulam — boundless; ruruduh — wept; cha — and; taptah — burning; shoka-arditah — racked with grief; vimanasah — distraught; ati-kleshah — in great anguish; babhuvuh — became.

7Bhagavan crossed the divine river6 and went away. Learning of it, the foremost of the twice-born lost heart: they fell into boundless dismay and wept, burning with grief; racked with sorrow and distraught, they were worn down by anguish.

Verse 8

तान्सप्तमेऽह्नि परिनष्टत्विषो ह्यवाप
श्रीचन्द्रशेखरगुणाकररत्नवर्यः।
आचार्यरत्नवरतप्तसुवर्णगौरः
कान्त्याक्षिपन्निव सुधाकरपूर्णशोभाम्॥८॥

tānsaptame'hni parinaṣṭatviṣo hyavāpa
śrīcandraśekharaguṇākararatnavaryaḥ|
ācāryaratnavarataptasuvarṇagauraḥ
kāntyākṣipanniva sudhākarapūrṇaśobhām||8||

tan — to them; saptame ahni — on the seventh day; parinashta-tvishah — whose lustre had vanished; hi — indeed; avapa — came; shri-chandrashekhara-guna-akara-ratna-varyah — Sri Chandrashekhara, a mine of virtues, an excellent jewel; acharyaratna — the Acharyaratna; vara-tapta-suvarna-gaurah — golden like fine molten gold; kantya — by his radiance; akshipan — eclipsing; iva — as if; sudhakara-purna-shobham — the beauty of the full moon.

8On the seventh day there came to them, who had lost all their lustre, Sri Chandrashekhara Acharyaratna, a mine of virtues, a jewel among men, golden like fine molten gold — by his radiance he seemed to eclipse the beauty of the full moon.

Verse 9

पप्रच्छुरब्जनयनस्य कथासुधां ते
तं तानुवाच तत्कथयामि सर्वम्।
कृष्णं सगद्गदगिरा द्विजवर्यमुख्यान्
श्रीचन्द्रशेखरधरामरवर्यमुख्यः॥९॥

papracchurabjanayanasya kathāsudhāṁ te
taṁ tānuvāca tatkathayāmi sarvam|
kṛṣṇaṁ sagadgadagirā dvijavaryamukhyān
śrīcandraśekharadharāmaravaryamukhyaḥ||9||

paprachchhuh — asked; abja-nayanasya — of the lotus-eyed; katha-sudham — for the nectar of the account; te — they; tam — him; tan — to them; uvacha — said; tat — that; kathayami — I shall tell; sarvam — all; krishnam — about Krishna; sa-gadgada-gira — with a voice choked with tears; dvija-varya-mukhyan — to the chief of the best of the twice-born; shri-chandrashekhara-dhara-amara-varya-mukhyah — Sri Chandrashekhara, foremost among the best of brahmanas.

9They asked him for the nectar of the account of the Lotus-eyed One, and he replied, "I shall tell you everything." And Sri Chandrashekhara, foremost among the best of brahmanas, in a voice choked with tears began to tell them of Krishna7.

Verse 10

गच्छद्विभोः पथि नरा वदनं निरीक्ष्य
नेत्रैः पपुः पुरुषभूषणगात्रशोभाम्।
न्यासाय तस्य गमनं च पुनर्विदित्वा
हृष्टाः प्रणेमुरमुमम्बुजपादयुग्मम्॥१०॥

gacchadvibhoḥ pathi narā vadanaṁ nirīkṣya
netraiḥ papuḥ puruṣabhūṣaṇagātraśobhām|
nyāsāya tasya gamanaṁ ca punarviditvā
hṛṣṭāḥ praṇemuramumambujapādayugmam||10||

gachchhat-vibhoh — of the Lord as He went; pathi — on the road; narah — people; vadanam — the face; nirikshya — gazing at; netraih — with their eyes; papuh — drank; purusha-bhushana-gatra-shobham — the beauty of the body of the ornament of men; nyasaya — for sannyasa; tasya — His; gamanam — going; cha — and; punah — then; viditva — learning; hrishtah — joyful; pranemuh — bowed; amum — to Him; ambuja-pada-yugmam — (to His) pair of lotus feet.

10"As the Lord walked along the road, people gazed at His face and drank with their eyes the beauty of the body of Him who is the ornament of men; and learning that He was going to take sannyasa, they joyfully bowed down at His lotus feet.

Verse 11

ननर्त तस्मिन्भगवान्मुकुन्दः
प्रेमार्द्रवक्षाः पुलकाचिताङ्गः।
हृष्टा जगुः कृष्णपदाब्जगीत-
माचार्यरत्नप्रमुखा महत्तमाः॥११॥

nanarta tasminbhagavānmukundaḥ
premārdravakṣāḥ pulakācitāṅgaḥ|
hṛṣṭā jaguḥ kṛṣṇapadābjagīta-
mācāryaratnapramukhā mahattamāḥ||11||

nanarta — danced; tasmin — there; bhagavan — Bhagavan; mukundah — Mukunda; prema-ardra-vakshah — His chest wet with (the tears of) love; pulaka-achita-angah — His body covered with thrills of rapture; hrishtah — joyful; jaguh — sang; krishna-pada-abja-gitam — a song of Krishna's lotus feet; acharyaratna-pramukhah — headed by the Acharyaratna; mahattamah — the great souls.

11There Bhagavan Mukunda8 danced, His chest wet with the tears of love, His body covered with thrills of rapture, while the great souls headed by the Acharyaratna joyfully sang a song of Krishna's lotus feet.

Verse 12

तस्मिन्क्षणे कण्टकनामपुर्यां
समागता ब्राह्मणसज्जनोत्तमाः।
नार्यश्च बालाश्च सुहृष्टवृद्धा
गृहीतहस्ता बधिरान्धकुब्जाः॥१२॥

tasminkṣaṇe kaṇṭakanāmapuryāṁ
samāgatā brāhmaṇasajjanottamāḥ|
nāryaśca bālāśca suhṛṣṭavṛddhā
gṛhītahastā badhirāndhakubjāḥ||12||

tasmin kshane — at that moment; kantaka-nama-puryam — in the town called Kantaka; samagatah — gathered; brahmana-sajjana-uttamah — the best of brahmanas and good people; naryah — women; cha — and; balah — children; cha — and; su-hrishta-vriddhah — the elders full of joy; grihita-hastah — led by the hand; badhira-andha-kubjah — the deaf, the blind and the hunchbacked.

12At that moment, in the town called Kantaka, there gathered the best of brahmanas and good folk, women, children and elders full of joy; the deaf, the blind and the hunchbacked were led there by the hand.

Verse 13

स्त्रियश्च काश्चिद्धृतपूर्णकुम्भा
धृतार्चनाः कक्षतटेषु काश्चित्।
काश्चिद्वयस्याधृतबाहुयुग्माः
सम्पूर्णगर्भास्त्वरितं समीयुः॥१३॥

striyaśca kāściddhṛtapūrṇakumbhā
dhṛtārcanāḥ kakṣataṭeṣu kāścit|
kāścidvayasyādhṛtabāhuyugmāḥ
sampūrṇagarbhāstvaritaṁ samīyuḥ||13||

striyah — women; cha — and; kashchit — some; dhrita-purna-kumbhah — carrying full pitchers; dhrita-archanah — carrying articles of worship; kaksha-tateshu — on their hips; kashchit — some; kashchit — some; vayasya-adhrita-bahu-yugmah — their arms supported by friends; sampurna-garbhah — heavy with child; tvaritam — in haste; samiyuh — came together.

13The women too came hurrying: some carrying full pitchers, some with articles of worship on their hips, and some, heavy with child, supported under the arms by their friends.

Verse 14

पपुर्हि सन्तप्तहृदस्तु सर्वा
जनार्दनस्याम्बुजवक्त्रसीधुम्।
बालार्कमिश्रं हि सुवर्णपद्म-
मिवापरा वीक्ष्य सुविस्मितास्ताः॥१४॥

papurhi santaptahṛdastu sarvā
janārdanasyāmbujavaktrasīdhum|
bālārkamiśraṁ hi suvarṇapadma-
mivāparā vīkṣya suvismitāstāḥ||14||

papuh — drank; hi — indeed; santapta-hridah — with burning hearts; tu — and; sarvah — all; janardanasya — of Janardana; ambuja-vaktra-sidhum — the honey-wine of the lotus face; bala-arka-mishram — blended with the young sun; hi — indeed; suvarna-padmam — a golden lotus; iva — like; aparah — others; vikshya — seeing; su-vismitah — amazed; tah — they.

14All of them, with burning hearts, drank the honey-wine of Janardana's lotus face; and others, gazing at Him as at a golden lotus blended with the young sun, could not cease to marvel.

Verse 15

ऊचुश्च कस्यायमपूर्वदर्शनः
समुद्यदिन्दुप्रतिमाननाभः।
शुभाय लोकस्य भवाय जातो
मात्रास्य पुण्येन धृतः स्वगर्भे॥१५॥

ūcuśca kasyāyamapūrvadarśanaḥ
samudyadindupratimānanābhaḥ|
śubhāya lokasya bhavāya jāto
mātrāsya puṇyena dhṛtaḥ svagarbhe||15||

uchuh — said; cha — and; kasya — whose; ayam — this; apurva-darshanah — of unprecedented aspect; samudyat-indu-pratima-anana-abhah — the radiance of whose face is like the rising moon; shubhaya — for the good; lokasya — of the world; bhavaya — for the welfare; jatah — born; matra — by the mother; asya — his; punyena — through (her) merit; dhritah — borne; sva-garbhe — in her womb.

15And they said, 'Whose is this youth, such as was never seen before, whose face shines like the rising moon? He was born for the good and the welfare of the world; surely it was through great merit that His mother bore Him in her womb.

Verse 16

असौ कुमारो जितकामदेवः
कान्त्या गिरा निर्जितवाक्पतिः शुभः।
भार्यास्य केनापि सुकर्मणाभूत्
केनापि का वा विरहातुरा स्फुटम्॥१६॥

asau kumāro jitakāmadevaḥ
kāntyā girā nirjitavākpatiḥ śubhaḥ|
bhāryāsya kenāpi sukarmaṇābhūt
kenāpi kā vā virahāturā sphuṭam||16||

asau — this; kumarah — youth; jita-kama-devah — who has conquered Kamadeva; kantya — by beauty; gira — by speech; nirjita-vak-patih — who has surpassed the lord of speech; shubhah — handsome; bharya — the wife; asya — his; kena api — by some; su-karmana — good deed; abhut — became; kena api — by some (deed); ka va — which woman; viraha-atura — is pining in separation; sphutam — plainly.

16This handsome youth has conquered Kamadeva with His beauty and surpassed the very lord of speech9 with His words. Some woman, by her good deeds, became His wife — and by some deeds, it seems, she now pines in separation!

Verse 17

मातास्य पुत्रस्य मुखं न दृष्ट्वा
जीवत्यजीवा बहुदुःखतप्ता।
यथा हि कृष्णो मथुरां दिदृक्षु-
र्गतो व्रजस्थाश्च बभूवुरार्ताः॥१७॥

mātāsya putrasya mukhaṁ na dṛṣṭvā
jīvatyajīvā bahuduḥkhataptā|
yathā hi kṛṣṇo mathurāṁ didṛkṣu-
rgato vrajasthāśca babhūvurārtāḥ||17||

mata — the mother; asya — of this; putrasya — son; mukham — the face; na drishtva — not seeing; jivati — lives; ajiva — lifeless; bahu-duhkha-tapta — burning with many sorrows; yatha — as; hi — indeed; krishnah — Krishna; mathuram — Mathura; didrikshuh — wishing to see; gatah — went; vraja-sthah — the people of Vraja; cha — and; babhuvuh — became; artah — stricken.

17His mother, not seeing her son's face, lives on as one lifeless, burning with many sorrows — as the people of Vraja grieved when Krishna went away, wishing to see Mathura.'

Verse 18

काश्चिद्विदग्धाः स्फुटमेव चाहु-
र्गोपाङ्गनाभावविभावितोऽसौ।
श्रीनन्दपुत्रः स्वयमाविरासी-
त्सन्न्यासवेशेन स्वकार्यसाधकः॥१८॥

kāścidvidagdhāḥ sphuṭameva cāhu-
rgopāṅganābhāvavibhāvito'sau|
śrīnandaputraḥ svayamāvirāsī-
tsannyāsaveśena svakāryasādhakaḥ||18||

kashchit — some; vidagdhah — discerning; sphutam eva — plainly; cha — and; ahuh — said; gopa-angana-bhava-vibhavitah — imbued with the feelings of the cowherd women; asau — this; shri-nanda-putrah — the son of Sri Nanda; svayam — Himself; avirasit — has appeared; sannyasa-veshena — in the dress of a sannyasi; sva-karya-sadhakah — accomplishing His own purpose.

18And others, more discerning, said plainly, 'This is the son of Sri Nanda Himself, imbued with the feelings of the cowherd women, who has appeared in the dress of a sannyasi to accomplish His own purpose.'

Verse 19

एवंविधान्या बहुधा सुवाचो
बभूवुरन्योन्यकथाप्रसङ्गैः।
मुखं पिबन्त्यो न विदुः स्वदेहं
विश्वम्भरस्याम्बुजलोचनस्य॥१९॥

evaṁvidhānyā bahudhā suvāco
babhūvuranyonyakathāprasaṅgaiḥ|
mukhaṁ pibantyo na viduḥ svadehaṁ
viśvambharasyāmbujalocanasya||19||

evam-vidhah — such; anyah — other; bahudha — many; su-vachah — fair words; babhuvuh — arose; anyonya-katha-prasangaih — in their talk with one another; mukham — the face; pibantyah — drinking in; na viduh — were unaware; sva-deham — of their own bodies; vishvambharasya — of Vishvambhara; ambuja-lochanasya — the lotus-eyed.

19Many such fair words and others besides passed in their talk with one another; drinking in the face of lotus-eyed Vishvambhara, they forgot their own bodies."

Thus ends the first sarga, "The Words of the Women of Kantakanagara" (Kantakanagara-nagari-vachana), of the third prakrama of the poem "Sri Krishna-chaitanya-charitamrita."

✦

Notes

  1. Damodara Pandita, who questions Murari: the poem is framed as their dialogue.
  2. Purushottama is Puri, the city of Jagannatha.
  3. The syntax of the second half of the verse is not entirely clear; the translation gives the probable sense.
  4. "Brahman" here means the spiritual, transcendent nature of Bhagavan Himself (cf. Bhagavad-gita 10.12, where Arjuna calls Krishna "the Supreme Brahman"), not an impersonal principle standing above Him: the impersonal Brahman rests on the Lord (ibid. 14.27).
  5. Shankara is Shiva.
  6. The Ganga.
  7. The reading is conjectural.
  8. Mukunda is here a name of the Lord Himself.
  9. The lord of speech is Brihaspati, the preceptor of the gods.
